segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon
segments.text: Ladies and gentlemen, African creativity has never been so visible. Our music is being exported. Our cinema is renewing the stories of ours, and our fashion is inspiring.

segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon
segments.text: However, one question remains, who controls the economic value it generates? segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon
segments.text: We do not build public policies on what we do not measure. It is then important to facilitate access to financing, by instruments that recognize the value of works and rights. The protection of creators constitutes the third requirement.

segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon
segments.text: Transparency in management, and fair remuneration, including in the era of platforms and artificial intelligence. This also means to pass on our heritage and invest in skills. Finally, in the concern of not leaving any talent at risk, the free-trade zone, African continent must become a real weapon.

segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon
segments.text: The free-trade zone is a market for our works and our artists. Under the impulse of His Excellency Brice Clotaire Oligingema, President of the Republic, Head of State, Head of the Gabonese Government, Gabon has committed to the structuring of its cultural sector. We have adopted a status of the artist and the cultural actor, launched the review of professionals in view of a national register, and undertook the reform of copyright management.

segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon
segments.text: The relaunch of YouthConnekt Gabon helps our young people to make their talent a business. This year, our creators have carried this ambition on demanding stages. Gabon was the country invited to the FEMUA in Abidjan, present at the African seminar of UNESCO in Paris.

segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon
segments.text: Each time, it is young talents, nourished by our traditions, who have carried the image of our country. This national effort does not hinder our commitment to African cooperation. Gabon will also carry in the YouthConnekt Africa instances the proposal of an African cooperation framework on cultural and creative industries, endowed with a network of incubators for young creators.

segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon
segments.text: Dear young people, Your heritage is not a burden, it is an advantage. It comes back to us to offer you a favorable environment, to protect your rights and to open your markets. It comes back to you to dare, to transmit and give the means to dare.

segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon
segments.text: This is, it seems to me, the meaning of the generational mission to which this summit invites us. segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon
segments.text: It is to tell you that today the future of Africa depends on you, on the ambition you have of your continent, on what you intend to do there. segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon

segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon

segments.speaker: Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture, Gabon

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: Your Excellency President Kagame, thank you for your kind invitation. I am, and Afrixen Bank is also honored to address the 8th YouthConnekt Africa Summit. Its focus on Africa's youth is a perfect fit with Afrixen Bank's own work for young entrepreneurs.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: That is why I see our participation as essential, even though I'm unable to join you in person. Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, the question before us is what Africa's youth stand to achieve when we finance them and build the ecosystem that invests in their talent and enables them to make dividend out of it. Never has that question been more urgent than now.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: In the past 10 years, Afrixen Bank has disbursed nearly $200 billion, largely to financial institutions and other corporates. It has also disbursed to governments in support of trade infrastructure and the development of special economic zones, amongst others. It did not take long to realize in doing this that these interventions had failed to reach our young people.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: Afrixen Bank therefore decided that a more effective way to reach the young is to invest in the creative economy. The creative economy, it seems, is where bankers and the youth meet with relative ease. We therefore established the Creative Africa Nexus Initiative, also known across the world and in Africa itself as CANEX, to which Afrixen Bank has committed over $2 billion to finance the film, music, design and fashion, arts and crafts, literature, sports, gastronomy, the theatre arts, new technologies and so on.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: Afrixen Bank's intervention has been in two ways. First, the infrastructure. We have invested and intend to continue to invest in recording studios, in arenas, exhibition centers and fashion factories Building the infrastructure is a long-term project.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: Our plan is to ensure that in each of the six sub-regions that make up Global Africa, a creative and cultural village is built, vibrant cities of innovation and creativity, great centers where wealth is created. The design and construction of the infrastructure is a steady process. It can sometimes be slow.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: So for that reason we decided that pending the construction of the infrastructure, we continue with the day-to-day business of investing in the talent itself. So our second intervention has been through financing. Talent needs funding to make the films.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: Talent needs funding to produce the music, organize the performances, sponsor the arts exhibitions, develop the technology applications and develop platforms to distribute the songs, the movies and even the brands that will take these creatives to the world markets. We intervened in small but pragmatic ways. It was often not by doing the complex things.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: It was by doing such simple things as providing financing or sponsorship to our designers to present their collections in Paris, in Porto, in New York, in Barcelona, in Lagos and elsewhere. We have acquired and commissioned more than 155 artworks by 71 African artists, displayed them across our own offices and offered them to great Africans. You might all have heard or watched the African film Clarissa.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: The Freixen Bank financed it and ensured that it premiered at the Cannes Festival in France. It was also screened at the Toronto International Film Festival in Canada in September of this year. Clarissa is intended to be projected in Marrakech at about now, perhaps yesterday, and released in cinemas across the world in the first quarter of next year.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: So did we invest in Muganga, another great African production from Congo, released in Cannes, in France and in Canada. We also recently entered into an arrangement with the Spanish great football club FC Barcelona for the production in Benin of their brand ware, to which we also display our own home brands. Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, never has a development been as critical as artificial intelligence.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: It has raised all stakes. It is changing how the world does business and where wealth is created and retained. We must invite you.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: We must invite the African youth to pay considerable attention to it and to the innovative industries generally. That is why we are investing in a software factory and innovation lab, creating opportunities for Africa's young talents to design and build technologies that can compete globally. To back it, in 2025, Afrikzimbang launched its first flagship accelerator program.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: Through that program, we are providing promising startups with access to investments of up to $250,000 each through our Fund for Export Development in Africa. That fund is located right there in Kigali. To go with the accelerator program, we have organized expert mentorships and strategic partnerships.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: The response has been remarkable, with over 1,600 applications from more than 40 African countries. And we are already seeing results. FinCard is one of them.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: It's an Egyptian-based small enterprise, one of our inaugural cohort startups. It went on to close an oversubscribed seed funding of around $2.8 million. Today, I'm pleased to announce the expansion of that Afrikzimbang flagship accelerator program.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: It's going to move from eight a year to 22 startups each year over the next several years. And over about five years, for example, we should have created 110 entrepreneurs, 110 serious, dedicated entrepreneurs across Africa and the Caribbean. And that is for our digital incubation program only.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: So to the African young innovators, our message is simple. We do not just want to finance your ideas. We want to build businesses that transcend borders, transform industries, drive African trade, and ultimately create wealth, for wealth creation is the objective.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: The next generation of global enterprises can and should also emerge from Africa and its diaspora. When you become the African entrepreneurs we would look up to, and who make us successful and proud, you would indeed have answered the call made by Frantz Fanon, an outstanding Pan-Africanist in his time, when he said over 60 years ago that each generation must, out of relative obscurity, discover its mission and fulfill it or betray it. You have discovered your mission.

segments.speaker: Afreximbank President (video message)
segments.text: African governments too, including Rwanda, have understood you. Afrixin Bank and other African financial institutions will help to fulfill it. Thank you for giving me this opportunity to address you.

segments.speaker: Joan Mazimhaka · Illume Studios
